lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: the triangle proportionality theorem

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

items.prompt: AB = 4 maps to DE = 12, BC = 5. Find EF.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: In a right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse divides it into segments of length 5 and 45. Find the altitude.
A 5 m pole casts a 2 m shadow. At the same moment a building casts a 6 m shadow. How tall is the building?
The Pythagorean theorem can be proved using similarity. Which statement correctly justifies it?
choices: The altitude to the hypotenuse creates two triangles similar to the original; writing both similarity proportions and adding them yields a² + b² = c².
The theorem follows from the triangle inequality.
Similarity gives a² + b² = c² only for isosceles right triangles.
The theorem follows because all right triangles are similar to each other.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF. Side AB = 10 corresponds to DE = 20. If BC = 5, find EF.
In a right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse divides it into segments of length 11 and 275. Find the altitude.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: A 4 m pole casts a 2 m shadow. At the same moment a building casts a 6 m shadow. How tall is the building?
A line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally. Which statement correctly justifies it?
choices: The parallel line bisects both sides by definition.
The two parts of each side are congruent because the line is parallel.
The result follows from the Pythagorean theorem applied twice.
The parallel line creates corresponding angles, giving a smaller triangle similar to the original by AA, so the sides are in proportion.
